title: NovaHealth POC scoping - quality eval plan
customer_attendees: Dr. Maria Gomez (Head of Data Science)
summary: AE+SE from Redwood ran a POC scoping focused on quality evaluation for NovaHealth's clinical summarization and triage workflows. Discussed success criteria (accuracy, hallucination rate, latency SLO), workload sizing (qps, avg/peak tokens), benchmark plan (golden prompts, regression tests, hallucination/format checks), scoring approach (automated heuristics + human rating), and timelines (pilot 4 weeks, benchmark by week 2). Agreed next steps: share golden prompt set and security docs, schedule benchmark run, and define success threshold for go/no-go.

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-27
Start: 14:00 PDT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee, Samir Patel (Redwood); Dr. Maria Gomez, Liam O'Connor, Priya Shah (NovaHealth)

Auto-summary (auto-generated may be rough):
- Scope: quality eval plan for POC focusing on clinical summarization + triage.
- Goal: define pass/fail, datasets, benchmarks, and timeline.

00:00 Speaker 1 (Jordan): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh quick roll call — Jordan Lee here from Redwood, Samir is with me, and we are excited to scope the POC for NovaHealth.
00:28 Speaker 2 (Dr. Gomez): Hi, Maria here, thanks. We are mainly focused on clinical note summarization and triage to route urgent cases. We want to evaluate quality before we move to production.
00:55 Speaker 1 (Jordan): Great, high level — what success looks like for you? like accuracy metrics, hallucination tolerance, latency?
01:10 Speaker 3 (Liam): For engineering, latency is important. We want 95th pct under 800 ms for single-note summarize, ideally lower. Cost is also a factor — we want to understand per-token.
01:30 Speaker 2 (Dr. Gomez): From clinical side accuracy: we need extractive accuracy above 92% on medication/diagnosis fields and hallucination rate below maybe 2% on critical items. We'll do human review for safety-critical ones.
01:50 Speaker 4 (Priya): Also output format matters. We need structured JSON outputs that our downstream EHR ingest can parse. Any formatting or hallucination we must catch.
02:08 Speaker 3 (Samir): Thanks, those are clear signals. For the POC we typically propose: a 4-week pilot, week 1 data ingest + integration, week 2 benchmark runs and golden prompts, week 3 regression/iterative tuning, week 4 final eval and runbook. Does that timeline align?
02:30 Speaker 2 (Dr. Gomez): Yes that seems doable. We can de-id and upload 200 representative notes by early next week.
02:48 Speaker 1 (Jordan): Perfect. Let's talk benchmarks: what tasks do we run — extraction, summarization, triage classification?
03:05 Speaker 2 (Dr. Gomez): All three. Extraction of meds/diagnoses, concise patient summary for clinicians, and a 3-way triage label (urgent / follow-up / routine).
03:25 Speaker 3 (Samir): Ok we'll build a test matrix. For each task we want golden prompts and ground truth. Ideally NovaHealth provides human-annotated ground truth for a subset for scoring.
03:45 Speaker 4 (Priya): We can provide human annotations for the 200 notes for the three tasks, but maybe only 50 fully annotated due to clinical reviewer time.
03:58 Speaker 1 (Jordan): That's fine — we can use 50 for scoring and the rest for broader tests. On scoring approach: we recommend automated metrics (F1/precision/recall for extraction, exact-match for some fields) plus a human rating rubric for overall quality and hallucination.
04:20 Speaker 2 (Dr. Gomez): Can you expand on hallucination checks? how do you detect those automatically?
04:30 Speaker 3 (Samir): Sure — we do a two-pronged approach: 1) exact entity match against ground truth for extraction tasks (flags missing/extra entities), 2) for summaries we run a hallucination detector heuristics plus spot human sampling. Heuristics include contradictions with source, improbable claims, and entity hallucination thresholds. Admittedly the auto detector is noisy, so human review remains important.
05:05 Speaker 2 (Dr. Gomez): ok noted. How about format checks? we need strict JSON schema validation and a fail-fast on unparsable outputs.
05:18 Speaker 1 (Jordan): Absolutely — our POC harness will validate schema, run regex checks for required fields, and flag parsability errors. We'll classify failures into hard failures (unparseable) and soft failures (missing non-critical fields).
05:40 Speaker 3 (Samir): On model selection: we can test a few open models we host — quantized variants for cost optimization, plus a higher-accuracy non-quantized baseline. We'll also run on Redwood Dedicated and show latency/cost tradeoffs.
05:58 Speaker 2 (Dr. Gomez): Are there privacy options? we need HIPAA-sensitive handling and KMS for keys. Also can we run on a private deployment?
06:12 Speaker 1 (Jordan): Yes — we support Private (VPC/on-prem) and Dedicated reserved capacity. For the pilot we usually run on Hosted or Dedicated depending on throughput; we can provide SOC2 and encryption docs. We'll attach security whitepaper.
06:30 Speaker 4 (Priya): Great. For integration, what does the ingest look like? we have FHIR wrapper and S3 exports.
06:40 Speaker 3 (Samir): We can read from S3 or pull via a secure endpoint. For POC, S3 with temporary credentials is easiest. We'll provide upload instructions.
06:55 Speaker 2 (Dr. Gomez): Workload sizing — our average note length is ~800 tokens after conversion; peak is about 40 qps during business hours but typical qps is 8-10. Concurrency peaks to maybe 25.
07:15 Speaker 1 (Jordan): Good to know. We'll propose a benchmark matrix that includes average 800-token requests at 10 qps and a peak scenario 40 qps with batching behavior measured. Also include cold vs warm start for KV cache.
07:38 Speaker 3 (Samir): For batching policies we'll run several settings: low-latency mode (small batch sizes, target 95th <800 ms), cost-optimized mode (larger batch sizes, measure tail latency), and a caching-enabled run to show cost savings.
07:58 Speaker 2 (Dr. Gomez): On scoring — can you give an example rubric for summaries?
08:05 Speaker 1 (Jordan): Sure — automated: ROUGE/ROUGE-L + embedding-similarity as a soft score; extractive F1 for key fields. Human rubric: 1-5 scale across accuracy, completeness, and hallucination risk. We'll combine via weighted sum; for pass we'd require overall >=3.8 and hallucination rate <=2% on critical entities.
08:38 Speaker 4 (Priya): Who will do the human ratings? internal NovaHealth reviewers or Redwood annotators?
08:45 Speaker 3 (Samir): We recommend NovaHealth clinical reviewers for final judgement, but Redwood can provide annotation support if you want consistency and speed (extra cost).
09:00 Speaker 2 (Dr. Gomez): We probably will use a mix — internal for critical subset, Redwood for bulk. We'll confirm.
09:12 Speaker 1 (Jordan): Ok. Let's talk about success criteria in plain language so it's unambiguous for sign-off. Suggested: 1) Extraction F1 >= 0.92 on the 50 annotated notes, 2) Summary average human score >=3.8/5, 3) Hallucination on critical entities <=2%, 4) 95th pct latency < 800ms on Dedicated at target throughput. Any objections?
09:40 Speaker 2 (Dr. Gomez): That matches clinical expectations. We might relax latency slightly if accuracy gains are significant.
09:50 Speaker 3 (Liam): We want to see a cost model though — per 1k tokens cost on each configuration.
09:58 Speaker 1 (Jordan): Yep we'll provide estimated TCO for hosted vs dedicated vs quantized models based on your expected monthly volume.
10:08 Speaker 4 (Priya): On hallucination regression tests — will we keep a golden prompt set and run nightly checks?
10:17 Speaker 3 (Samir): For the POC we suggest nightly regression against the golden prompts for the duration and a final regression run at end. Golden prompts will include edge cases we provide and negative examples to catch hallucination.
10:34 Speaker 2 (Dr. Gomez): Can you show an example golden prompt?
10:40 Speaker 1 (Jordan): Example: "Summarize the following clinical note into a 3-sentence discharge summary focusing on diagnosis, meds, and next steps. Return JSON with keys: summary, diagnoses[], medications[]." We'll capture strict schema and an example expected output.
10:58 Speaker 3 (Samir): We'll also include mutation tests: slight paraphrases and redactions to ensure robustness and to check for hallucinations when info is missing.
11:10 Speaker 2 (Dr. Gomez): How are regression failures triaged?
11:15 Speaker 1 (Jordan): We'll classify into model-related, prompt-tuning related, and ingestion/format failures. Each failure produces a support ticket with stack traces and sample inputs/outputs.
11:30 Speaker 3 (Samir): One practical point — tokenization variance across models affects cost numbers. We'll normalize counts using the specific tokenizer per model in the benchmark.
11:45 Speaker 2 (Dr. Gomez): Are you able to run a hallucination detection metric like fact-F1?
11:50 Speaker 3 (Samir): We can compute fact-oriented F1 for entities we care about; for free text claims it's harder but we can approximate with embedding and entailment checks against source. Expect that to be noisy but useful as a signal.
12:08 Speaker 4 (Priya): Regarding the POC environment, do we need specific network whitelisting?
12:15 Speaker 1 (Jordan): For Hosted no whitelists typically, but for Dedicated/Private we'll need IP allowlists or peered VPC. We'll send network requirements doc.
12:30 Speaker 2 (Dr. Gomez): Ok timeline recap?
12:35 Speaker 1 (Jordan): Week 0 (this week): dataset de-id + upload; Week 1: integration & initial runs; Week 2: benchmark matrix and golden prompts + first benchmark; Week 3: tuning and regression; Week 4: final eval, runbook, sign-off decision.
12:58 Speaker 3 (Liam): That timeline is ok if we can get the annotated 50 notes quickly.
13:05 Speaker 2 (Dr. Gomez): We'll prioritize those 50 and send them by Monday.
13:12 Speaker 1 (Jordan): Good. Any compliance questions?
13:18 Speaker 4 (Priya): We need to confirm data retention policy for Hosted runs and whether logs are retained.
13:25 Speaker 1 (Jordan): We'll include retention options in the security doc; Dedicated/Private give more control.
13:35 Speaker 3 (Samir): I'll note for benchmark: we'll run with retention disabled for test data unless you request otherwise.
13:45 Speaker 2 (Dr. Gomez): What about model rollbacks and A/B testing for production?
13:50 Speaker 1 (Jordan): Redwood supports canary rollouts and automatic fallback to previous model versions; we'll include rollout plan in the runbook if you move to Dedicated.
14:05 Speaker 4 (Priya): One last question — can you demonstrate hallucination cases we should watch out for?
14:10 Speaker 3 (Samir): We can prepare a short demo video showing examples and common failure modes in the follow-up demo.
14:25 Speaker 1 (Jordan): Ok to recap actions: Jordan sends golden prompts + security docs; Samir prepares benchmark config and schedule; NovaHealth provides 200 notes and 50 annotated. We reconvene in one week.
14:40 Speaker 2 (Dr. Gomez): Sounds good, thanks everyone.
14:44 Speaker 1 (Jordan): Thanks all — end.

Post-call notes (auto):

- Follow-up items captured above.
